edits.original_quote: Our results suggest that increasing financial rewards rarely produces large performance gains in the experimental settings most studied by economists.
edits.inserted_text: Because this literature tends, by design, to avoid contexts where incentives are expected to have large effects (Section 3), we read this as a statement about the contexts economists have chosen to study rather than about incentive effectiveness in general.

edits.original_quote: The Bayesian approach, however, treats all observations as independent, and to account for within-study dependence we also employ frequentist model averaging with Mallow's weights (Hansen, 2007) and orthogonalization of model space according to Amini & Parmeter (2012).
edits.inserted_text: Because most studies contribute many correlated estimates, we treat the dependence-aware frequentist averaging as the primary basis for our heterogeneity conclusions and report the Bayesian inclusion probabilities alongside it for comparison.
